description:
Sound and Scribble is a playgroup built around five stations - sound, scribble, structure, súgradh (play) and sensory - giving babies and toddlers a varied, hands-on session each week. It runs on Fridays from 9.30 to 10.30am in the Scouts Den, Castlebar, at a cost of €10 per session.

Mums, dads, grandparents and other caregivers are all welcome to bring their little ones along, though supervision is required for the full session. Expect a messy play station most weeks, so a change of clothes is a good idea.

Held every Friday from 9.30 to 10.30am in the Scouts Den, Castlebar, Sound and Scribble is a playgroup for babies and toddlers structured around five themed stations: sound, scribble, structure, súgradh and sensory play. Sessions cost €10 each.

All caregivers - mothers, fathers, grandparents and childminders - are welcome to join in with their little ones, and an adult must stay for the whole session. Because messy play features regularly, it's worth packing a spare set of clothes.

Ardtreo Gymnastics Academy's Soft Play & GymTots is a relaxed, play-based session for babies, toddlers and preschoolers to explore movement safely. Soft mats, tunnels, balance beams, obstacle courses and music help build coordination, confidence and social skills, and it's entirely child-led - no gymnastics experience needed. All equipment is provided; bring soft-play-friendly clothing and a drink of water.

Mums, dads, grandparents, guardians and childminders are all welcome, along with siblings aged 0-5, and a caregiver must stay for the full session alongside the qualified coaches on hand.

Sessions run Fridays and Sundays in the afternoon at Kilmore Community Hub, Monaghan, H18 HY65 (easy parking, pram-friendly access), at €8.50 per soft play session.

This Soft Play & GymTots session at Kilmore Community Hub gives children aged 0-5 a child-led, open-play environment to move, climb and explore alongside a parent or carer. It's less about formal gymnastics and more about confidence-building through free play - a good option for younger siblings not yet ready for structured classes.

Sessions run on Fridays and Sundays, cost €8.50 per visit, and a caregiver is expected to stay for the full session throughout.

La Leche League runs mother-to-mother breastfeeding support in Monaghan, open to pregnant and breastfeeding mums along with their babies and toddlers - and a good place to meet other local parents. The Doohamlet Community Centre session, Dernaglug, Co. Monaghan (A75 EF99), meets every second Thursday at 10.30am and is free to attend.

A second monthly session runs at the Hillgrove Hotel, Old Armagh Rd, Latlorcan, Monaghan (H18 RK15), every fourth Wednesday at 10.30am, also free. For either session, contact lalecheleaguemonaghan@gmail.com.

La Leche League Monaghan offers mother-to-mother breastfeeding support and information, welcoming pregnant and breastfeeding mums with their babies and toddlers in tow. The Hillgrove Hotel session, Old Armagh Rd, Latlorcan, Monaghan (H18 RK15), runs every fourth Wednesday at 10.30am and is free.

There's also a fortnightly session at Doohamlet Community Centre, Dernaglug, Co. Monaghan (A75 EF99), held every second Thursday at 10.30am. Email lalecheleaguemonaghan@gmail.com for details on either group.

This baby massage and reflexology course in Carrickmacross, Co. Monaghan runs over a 4-week term, with 1 to 1.5 hour sessions from 10 to 11.30am. It gives parents dedicated one-on-one bonding time with their baby while learning routines that can bring lasting benefits for digestive, respiratory, sleep, teething and general wellbeing.

The approach is baby-led and no-stress - feeding, changing and even sleeping are all fine mid-session - with hands-on practice guided by a qualified instructor, plus take-home notes and diagrams. Each session ends with time for sensory and social connection. Cost: €60.

Moo Music's Carrickmacross classes bring together singing, movement and instrument play for children from newborn through to age 5, drawing on a bank of 125 original songs written specifically for early-years music sessions.

Music and movement at this age is widely recognised to support language development, rhythm and coordination, as well as giving parents and little ones a fun, shared activity together each week.

Sinead Grace's baby massage classes in Birr, Co. Offaly run at the County Arms Hotel on Thursdays at 11am, starting 15th January - a block of 5 classes for €150, including hotel tea and coffee (up to €100 may be reclaimable through private health insurance). A companion group runs at the GAA Club in Toomevara, Co. Tipperary, Thursdays at 10.30am, for €125 per block.

Across the 5 weeks you'll learn a full-body massage routine plus techniques for easing colic, gas and constipation, strokes that support relaxation and digestion, and how to read your baby's cues - building digestion, calmer sleep, bonding and parent confidence along the way.

Contact Sinead Grace on 086 2514700 or @babymassagesineadgrace on Instagram.

In Toomevara, Co. Tipperary, Sinead Grace runs baby massage classes at the GAA Club on Thursdays at 10.30am, €125 for a block of 5 classes with tea and coffee included (up to €100 may be reclaimable through private health insurance). A sister group meets at the County Arms Hotel in Birr, Co. Offaly on Thursdays at 11am, from €150 per block.

Each block covers a full-body massage routine, techniques to ease colic, gas and constipation, strokes for relaxation and digestion, and reading your baby's cues - supporting calmer sleep, easier digestion and stronger bonding.

Contact Sinead Grace on 086 2514700, or find her on Instagram at babymassagesineadgrace.

Kids Connect Sligo blends children's yoga, mindfulness arts and crafts, and mindfulness Lego into one-hour sessions built for ages 4-15, running as 6-week terms for €75. Each class opens with movement - an obstacle course covering gross motor skills and balance - followed by a group 'best bit of the week' round that builds an attitude of gratitude.

Three yoga poses are practised each week alongside pranayama breathing exercises using feathers, bubbles, a light ball and straws, plus dance, move and freeze songs from Kidding Around Yoga. Classes wind down with a mindfulness story and activities from Louise Shannaher, mindfulness colouring, Lego, and the closing 'Peace Begins with Me' song.

Combining mindfulness, arts and crafts, Lego and children's yoga, Kids Connect Sligo runs one-hour classes for ages 4 to 15 across 6-week terms (€75). Each session finishes with mindfulness colouring, Lego play, a story from Louise Shannaher and the group's closing 'Peace Begins with Me' song.

Earlier in the class, children work through an obstacle course for gross motor skills and balance, share a 'best bit of the week' to build gratitude, and practise three yoga poses along with pranayama breathing games using feathers, bubbles, a light ball and straws - plus dance, move and freeze songs from Kidding Around Yoga.

Strandhill Parent and Toddler Group is a voluntary, community-run group for local parents, guardians and childminders with babies or toddlers to drop in for a chat, a cup of tea and some toys and snacks for the kids. It meets every Wednesday from 10.30am to 12pm during the school term, for €3 per family.

The group originally met upstairs in Strandhill Celtic Football Club, Carrowbunnaun (next to the playground on Airport Rd), where there's buggy space at the bottom of the stairs but no lift. As of January 2025 it operates from The Surf Centre, Shore Rd, Carrowbunnaun, Strandhill, Co. Sligo, F91 XH50. Contact 086 6038260 for more information.

Every Wednesday during the school term, from 10.30am to 12pm, Strandhill Parent and Toddler Group opens its doors to local families for a relaxed drop-in of tea, toys and conversation - all parents, guardians and childminders welcome, at €3 per family.

Since January 2025 the group has been based at The Surf Centre, Shore Rd, Carrowbunnaun, Strandhill, Co. Sligo, F91 XH50; it previously ran upstairs in Strandhill Celtic Football Club nearby (buggy space at the bottom of the stairs, though there's no lift). Call 086 6038260 for details.

Also known as Toddler Talk and Tea Time, this Tipperary parent, baby and toddler group meets at Annacarty Community Centre every Thursday from 9.30 to 10.30am during the school term - free to attend, with a cuppa, a chat and playtime for the little ones.

A sister session runs at Cappawhite National School, Cappagh, Co. Tipperary, E34 V598, every Wednesday during term time. The group's Facebook page is no longer actively updated, but both sessions continue to run - contact 087 3386923 for current details.

This Tipperary parent, baby and toddler group - also known as Toddler Talk and Tea Time - meets at Cappawhite National School, Cappagh, Co. Tipperary, E34 V598, every Wednesday during the school term, giving local parents and carers a free, informal spot to meet up while little ones play.

A second session runs at Annacarty Community Centre every Thursday from 9.30 to 10.30am, also during term time. Though the group's Facebook page is inactive, both sessions are still running - call 087 3386923 to check times.

Run by the Community Mothers Programme, this Mother and Baby Group welcomes all parents with children aged 0-5 across Cashel and Clonmel, Co. Tipperary. The Cashel session meets at Our Lady of Lourdes Hospital every Thursday from 10 to 11.30am, free of charge, with community mothers on hand to offer support and information.

A second free session runs in Clonmel at the Clonmel Resource Centre, Kickham St, every Monday from 2 to 3.30pm. Both are a relaxed way to meet other local mums and babies.

This Community Mothers Programme group gives parents of children aged 0-5 in Clonmel and Cashel, Co. Tipperary a free, supportive space to meet other mums and babies. The Clonmel session runs at Clonmel Resource Centre, Kickham St, every Monday from 2 to 3.30pm, with community mothers on hand for support and information.

A parallel free session meets in Cashel at Our Lady of Lourdes Hospital every Thursday from 10 to 11.30am.

Run by ARC (Adamstown/Raheen/Clonroche) Family Resource Centre, this Wexford parent and toddler group meets in Raheen Community Hall every Thursday from 9.30 to 11am during the school term, at €2 per family. Sessions mix activities, mindfulness, classes and presentations with plenty of time to connect with other local parents while the children make friends. Contact Rachel on 087 9669553 or Jayne on 089 4354670.

A sister group runs at Adamstown Community Centre every Friday, same times and price - contact Amanda on 089 4285037. All parents, guardians and childminders are welcome at either.

ARC (Adamstown/Raheen/Clonroche) Family Resource Centre runs this Wexford parent and toddler group at Adamstown Community Centre every Friday from 9.30 to 11am during term time, at €2 per family - contact Amanda on 089 4285037. Expect activities, mindfulness, classes and presentations alongside plenty of chances to connect with other local parents and for children to build friendships.

A parallel session runs at Raheen Community Hall every Thursday, same times and price - contact Rachel on 087 9669553 or Jayne on 089 4354670.

Dublin Zoo's Bricktacular workshops bring LEGO building to the Discovery and Learning Centre on select summer weekends, with 40-minute sessions for children aged 5 to 15. Tickets cost €27 per child, which includes a day's entry to the zoo.

It's a hands-on, creative way to combine a zoo day out with some construction play, suited to both first-time builders and confident brick fans.

Dublin Zoo's week-long summer camps for ages 7-12 run Monday to Friday, 10am to 2.30pm, with a focus on wildlife and conservation rather than direct animal contact. Children get an insider's look at the zoo's work while learning about the animals and habitats around them.

A week costs €170, or €155 for zoo annual pass holders.

Dublin Capoeira's Capoeira Kids classes, held at Marrowbone Lane in Saint Catherine's, Dublin 8, introduce children aged 5 to 11 to the fundamentals of this playful Brazilian martial art. Alongside kicks, sweeps and acrobatic movement, classes bring in the music, rhythm and cultural roots that set capoeira apart from other martial arts.

It's a good fit for kids who enjoy movement and music as much as physical challenge, building fitness, coordination and confidence along the way.

For families curious about capoeira before committing, Dublin Capoeira runs a 1-hour kids' trial class at Portmarnock Sports and Leisure Club, Blackwood Lane, Co. Dublin. It's a low-commitment way to sample this energetic Brazilian martial art, which blends kicks, acrobatics, music and rhythm.

The trial gives children a taste of the movement and games that make up regular capoeira classes before signing up for an ongoing term.

T45 Jiujitsu's Cork programme offers kids' Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu across two age groups: Little Ninjas for 4-7 year-olds and Juvenile Jiujitsu for 8-12 year-olds. Classes build coordination, discipline and self-defence fundamentals in a structured, supportive setting.

A free trial week is available for families who want to try a class before joining.

At Unit 1, Ballinacurra Business Park, Midleton, Co. Cork, T45 Jiujitsu runs kids' Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu classes split into Little Ninjas (ages 4-7) and Juvenile Jiujitsu (ages 8-12), led by Coach Laura Power. Sessions build coordination, discipline and self-defence skills through structured, age-appropriate training.

As with T45's other locations, a free trial week is available before committing to a term.

Artz For Kids runs an after-school art class at St Stephens School, Navan, Co. Meath for children aged 6-12, held from 4.20 to 5.40pm. It's a chance for kids to explore drawing, painting and craft techniques in a relaxed after-school setting, right on school grounds for easy pick-up.

This weekly illustration class at Dee Hub, Townparks, Co. Louth runs on Thursdays for children aged 5-12, giving young artists a regular space to build drawing skills, from basic techniques through to more developed illustration work. Artz for Kids runs the sessions in a supportive, small-group setting suited to varying skill levels.

Shoreline Leisure's children's swim lessons in Bray, Co. Wicklow run as progressive 8-week terms across Levels 1 to 5, for ages 4-12. Small class sizes mean qualified instructors can give each child focused attention as they build water confidence, stroke technique and safety skills.

Classes take place at the centre on Southern Cross Road, Bray.

Shoreline Leisure's Greystones Swim School offers a structured swimming programme for children aged 4 and up, building from foundational water confidence through to stronger stroke technique. Younger babies aren't left out either - a Parent & Tadpole class caters for 4 to 12 month-olds in the water with a parent.

For more advanced swimmers, there are pathways into lane training and junior lifeguard training, giving children a route to progress well beyond beginner level.

Metropolitan School of Dance teaches classical ballet from age 3 upwards, across multiple locations in Dublin and Kildare including Balbriggan and Leixlip. Classes build the posture, coordination and technique that underpin ballet, in a structured, age-graded programme suited to complete beginners as well as more experienced young dancers.

Metropolitan School of Dance runs classes at Burrow National School, Howth Road, Sutton, Dublin 13, for dancers from age 3 through to young adult - a separate venue from the school's existing Balbriggan/Leixlip location. As with the school's other branches, expect a structured, age-graded approach to building technique and confidence over time.

AKT Stage School's Athlone programme has been running since 2013, teaching drama, dance and music to children and teens aged 4-18. Alongside performance skills, classes put a strong emphasis on building self-esteem and a sense of belonging - as much about confidence and community as stagecraft.

AKT Stage School runs Friday performing arts classes at the Town Hall Theatre, Ballinasloe, Co. Galway, covering age groups from preschool through to 3rd Year. Classes combine drama, dance and music, with fees ranging from €180 to €230 per term depending on age group.

RINKA Kids Fitness runs weekly sessions for ages 5-12 at Errigal College, Letterkenny, on Tuesdays from 6.15 to 7pm. Classes combine cardio and strength-based games with a focus on overall wellbeing, giving children a structured, fun way to build fitness habits outside of school sport.

At the Kilmore Centre, Dublin Road, Cavan, RINKA Kids Fitness (run through Fit Forever Cavan) offers weekly Tuesday sessions split by age into 3-4, 5-7 and 8+ groups, running from September through June. Each group's activities are pitched to the children's stage of development, building fitness and coordination through games rather than formal training.

Playful Tribe's afterschool art clubs run from a home-studio setting in Bettystown, Co. Meath, on Mondays and Tuesdays, with all materials provided. It's a drop-off session where children can settle into creative, process-led art-making without needing extra support from a parent on-site.

This one-off pop-up morning from Playful Tribe combines art and movement for children aged 4-10 at Halla na Féile, Cashel, Co. Tipperary. Activities include t-shirt decorating alongside crafts and games, giving kids a mix of creative and active play in a single session, for €25 per child.

Alto School of Music runs after-school ukulele group lessons for pupils of Templerainey NS and St. Joseph's in Arklow, Co. Wicklow, held on Mondays straight after the school day. It's an easy entry point into music-making, with the ukulele's small size and simple chord shapes making it a popular first instrument for children.

Alto School of Music delivers group and private lessons in piano, guitar, violin and other instruments directly inside local primary schools around Ranelagh, Dublin 6, for children roughly aged 5-12. Lessons taking place on school grounds make it straightforward to fit music tuition around the school day, whether a child is starting an instrument for the first time or continuing on from previous lessons.

Lets Go Kids Camps runs a summer camp at Dunboyne Community Centre, Co. Meath, from 9.30am to 3.30pm each day, with prices from €100 to €130 per child depending on the week and sibling discounts. Expect a full day of varied activities and games designed to keep kids active and engaged through the summer break.

At Comeragh College, Carrick-on-Suir, Co. Tipperary, Lets Go Kids Camps runs a summer camp from 9.30am to 3.30pm daily, giving children a full day of structured activities and games during the school holidays.

Little Kickers County Galway runs its football classes for young children on Saturday mornings at the Emerald Ballroom, McNevin Ave, Ballinasloe, split across Little Kicks, Junior Kickers and Mighty Kickers age groups. Each group builds football skills and coordination through games rather than drills, suited to children at different stages from toddler through to early school age.

Little Kickers County Galway's Loughrea classes run on Sunday mornings at Temperance Hall, for children aged 1.5 to 5. Sessions use games and play rather than formal drills to introduce football skills, coordination and teamwork at an age-appropriate pace.

Junior Einsteins runs an 8-week hands-on STEM afterschool club for 1st to 6th class children at St Josephs Hall, Blessington Village, Co. Wicklow, on Wednesdays, for €100. Each week brings a new set of experiments and activities designed to make science tangible and fun outside the classroom.

Junior Einsteins' Junior Chemists science camp, held at Monasterevin Community Centre, Co. Kildare, gives children aged 5-11 a hands-on introduction to chemistry and engineering concepts through experiments and building activities, run in a camp format during school holidays.

Ruth Shine School of Dance teaches classical ballet at DanceTrax Studios, Unit 6 Upper, Blessington Shopping Centre, with dedicated boys-only classes as well as a Wobblers and Toddlers option for the youngest dancers. It's a structured introduction to ballet technique, with class groupings tailored to age and experience.

With more than 30 years running, Ruth Shine School of Dance's Palmerstown branch teaches dance from toddler age right through to adult, based at the Parish Centre in Palmerstown village, Dublin 20. That long track record means an established, age-graded programme for dancers at every stage, from first steps to more advanced technique.

StageSchool Ireland's Rathgar classes run on Saturday mornings at The High School, Danum, Zion Road, for children and teens aged 4-18. Each session rotates through singing, dance and drama, giving young performers a well-rounded introduction to musical theatre across all three disciplines.

At Rathdown School, Upper Glenageary Road, Glenageary, Co. Dublin, StageSchool Ireland runs musical theatre classes for ages 4-18 that rotate through singing, dance and drama - the same well-rounded format as the school's Rathgar branch, in a separate south Dublin venue.

Sean Gilligan Performing Arts teaches drama, dance and music at Star Studios, Kilbarrack Shopping Centre, Swan's Nest Road, Dublin 5, for children aged 3 and up. Classes give young performers a broad grounding across all three performing arts disciplines rather than specialising in just one.

Sean Gilligan Performing Arts runs a separate branch in Artane, Dublin 5, offering the same drama, dance and music classes as the company's Kilbarrack studio, split into Junior and Intermediate groups for children aged 3-13.

Doodlebox runs inclusive art classes for primary school children at Rua Red South Dublin Arts Centre, Blessington Road, Tallaght, Dublin 24, led by a qualified art therapist. Children work across a wide range of media and materials, building skills over the term towards an annual student exhibition.

Classes are split by age into Doodle Bugs (5-8 years) and Doodle Buddies (9-12 years), with multiple weekly slots on Thursdays (3.30pm, 4.30pm, 6pm and 7.15pm) and Saturdays (10am, 11.15am, 12.30pm, 1.45pm and 3.15pm). Each student gets a 'Doodle Bag' of art materials every term, and the new term begins Wednesday 9th September 2026.

The venue is wheelchair and buggy accessible, with an on-site café and changing facilities - a drop-off class for parents happy to leave children in for the session.

Wild by Nature Forest School runs family sessions in the woodland at Cabinteely Park (Bray Road entrance), Cabinteely, Dublin 18, with activities including wild crafts, rope swings and bridges, scavenger hunts, wild food exploration and games for all ages. Sessions run as recurring multi-week blocks - a 7-week Monday afternoon block has run previously.

These are parent-accompanied sessions, so the whole family gets involved together rather than dropping children off. Booking directly by email is worth doing, as it avoids a separate booking fee that can apply when booking through Eventbrite. Free parking is available at the park.

Lucan School of Music offers individual instrumental lessons at Coláiste Phádraig CBS, Roselawn, Lucan, Co. Dublin, for students from pre-school age right through to adult. Over 500 students attend weekly across a range of instruments and skill levels, with a student-centred teaching approach and the option to prepare for grade exams.

Free parking is available at the venue; pricing isn't published online, so it's best to contact the school directly for current rates.

Dimples Baby Massage runs a certified 4-week baby massage course at Mount Merrion Community Centre, The Rise, Mount Merrion, Co. Dublin, for pre-crawling babies aged six weeks to eight months. Classes are led by a certified infant massage instructor and kept small, with a maximum of 8-10 babies per group.

The course costs €135 online (€150 standard rate) and is described by the provider as compatible with health insurance reimbursement. Each session wraps up with refreshments and social time, giving parents a chance to chat once class is done.

Play Cafe / Bumps and Babes is a parent and toddler group meeting every Wednesday from 10 to 11.30am in Kilternan, Dublin 18. It's an informal drop-in for parents and carers to bring their little ones along for playtime, a chat and some company with other local families.

Talls and Smalls meets every Wednesday afternoon, 3 to 4.30pm, at Urban Junction on Main Street, Blackrock, Co. Dublin. It's an indoor, informal parent and toddler group where local families can drop in for playtime and a chat, with no need to book ahead.

Baby Talk is a parent and toddler drop-in group held every Wednesday from 9.30 to 11.30am in Sandyford, Dublin 18, giving local parents and carers a relaxed weekly spot to bring their little ones for playtime and a chance to meet other families in the area.

Honey Bee Hive runs a weekly parent and toddler drop-in every Tuesday from 9.30 to 11am in Stillorgan, Co. Dublin - an easygoing session for local parents, carers and young children to play, socialise and get to know other families nearby.

Wobblers and Toddlers meets every Friday from 10am to 12pm at Balally Family Resource Centre, Sandyford, Dublin 16. It's a relaxed, drop-in parent and toddler session giving local families a two-hour window each week to play and socialise together.

Blackrock Library hosts a free parent and toddler group every Friday from 10.30am, giving local parents, carers and young children a regular, no-cost spot to play and meet other families within the library's indoor space.

Every Monday from 10.30 to 11.45am, Shankill Library runs a free drop-in parent and toddler group, offering local families an indoor space to socialise and let children play together during term and school holidays alike.

Dalkey Library runs a free parent and toddler group twice a week - Mondays and Fridays, 10.30 to 11.15am - giving local families more frequent opportunities than most library groups to drop in for informal playtime and a chat indoors.

Dundrum Library's parent and toddler group meets every Monday from 10am to 12pm, free to attend, offering a full two-hour indoor session for local parents, carers and young children to play and socialise together.

Every Monday from 10.30 to 11.30am, Deansgrange Library hosts a free drop-in parent and toddler group indoors, giving local families a regular weekly spot to bring young children along for play and informal socialising.

Ballyogan Community Development Group runs a free parent and toddler group every Tuesday from 10.30am to 12pm in Ballyogan, Dublin 18. As a community-run rather than library-based group, it gives local parents, carers and young children an indoor space to play and connect with neighbours.

Kidspace Rathfarnham's summer camp runs Monday to Friday, 9.30am to 2pm, for children aged 4-8 at Kidspace PlayCentre, 20 Main Street, Rathfarnham, Dublin. Days combine soft-play, arts and crafts, baking and games in a supervised indoor setting run by childcare professionals, with lunch, snacks and drinks included.

A full week costs €120 for a first child, dropping to €100 for a second sibling and €80 for further siblings; single day passes are also available at €30 (€24 with the National Childcare Scheme universal rate applied). The venue has free parking, an on-site café and changing facilities.

Ballyboden St Endas GAA, Camogie & Ladies Football Club runs its Campa Samhraidh summer camp Monday to Friday at Firhouse Road, Dublin 16, for primary school-age children (roughly 6-13). Coaching covers football, hurling and camogie skills through drills, small-sided games and team activities at one of Dublin's largest GAA clubs.

A week costs €70 for one child, or €130 combined for two. The club typically runs several camp weeks over the summer, though its 2026 week (17-21 August) was sold out at time of research - worth checking early for availability. Outdoor venue with free parking.

Bank of Ireland Leinster Rugby's summer camp runs Monday to Friday, 9.30am to 1.30pm, at Stillorgan-Rathfarnham RFC, Heavey Technology Park, Tibradden Road, Rathfarnham, Dublin 16, for children aged 6-12. IRFU-accredited Leinster Rugby coaches lead sessions covering passing, tackling, evasion and kicking for both boys and girls, with a kit pack included for those attending the full week.

Pricing for 2026 wasn't published at time of research, though recent years have seen weekly rates in the €75-90 range with reduced sibling/second-camp rates - best to confirm current pricing when booking. Outdoor venue, free parking.

Kilmacud Crokes GAA Club's summer programme at Glenalbyn House, Glenalbyn Road, Stillorgan, Co. Dublin, runs Monday to Friday and combines a Multi Sports Camp (GAA games plus tennis, basketball, rounders and more) with dedicated GAA Summer Camp weeks focused on football, hurling and camogie. Both are open to members and non-members.

Registration and current pricing run through the club's ClubForce booking system; camps have historically run across multiple weeks through July and August. The venue has both indoor and outdoor facilities, free parking and changing rooms on site.

Tallaght Leisure Centre, Fortunestown Way, Dublin 24, runs two swimming programmes for young children: Adult and Toddler Swim, a low-cost pay-as-you-go pool session for babies and toddlers from 4 months to 5 years, and structured Children's Swim Lessons for ages 3 and up, taught by qualified instructors across all ability levels, with lifeguards on duty throughout.

Toddler swim sessions can be paid for as you go - check the pool timetable for current times. Swim lessons require a minimum booking of 8 sessions, paid in full at booking, and parents or guardians must remain on site during lessons. The centre is wheelchair accessible with a café, changing facilities and free parking.

South Dublin Dance Academy, based at Tallaght Enterprise Centre, Main Road, Tallaght, Dublin 24, teaches Ballet, Hip Hop, Tap and Musical Theatre to children, teens and adults from age 3 up. Ballet builds posture, coordination and technical foundations that carry across other dance styles; Hip Hop focuses on contemporary choreography and rhythm; Tap develops footwork and timing; and Musical Theatre combines singing, dancing and acting, culminating in an annual showcase performance.

Current pricing and the weekly timetable are managed through the academy's online enrolment system.

Junior Einsteins runs an after-school science club inside Lycée Français International Samuel Beckett, Foxrock Avenue, Newpark, Foxrock, Co. Dublin, on Mondays and Thursdays from 3 to 4pm during the school term. Sessions use messy, high-energy experiments to build curiosity and early scientific thinking in young children.

Separate weekly groups run for Maternelle/Infant classes and for Year 1 & Year 2 pupils. Pricing for this in-school club isn't published online and is arranged directly with the school or provider.

Trojan Gymnastic Club, based at 7/8 Holly Avenue, Stillorgan Business Park, Blackrock, Co. Dublin, runs recreational gymnastics for children aged 3-12 across four progressive groups. Mini Rock 'n' Rollers and Rock 'n' Rollers introduce balance, coordination and basic shapes; Banana Splits builds towards bridge kick-overs, drop backs and round-offs; and Twisters works on walkovers, aerials and handsprings for children assessed as ready to progress.

Term pricing and class times are managed through the club's member booking portal; a Gymnastics Ireland membership fee applies to all new members. Free parking is available at the venue.

Dundrum South Dublin Athletic Club, based at Tibradden Road, Taylorsgrange, Dublin 16, is Ireland's largest athletics club and offers juvenile athletics training in track & field, cross country and road running for children from primary through secondary school age. Training takes place on the club's own 400m Mondo track and trail campus in the foothills of the Dublin mountains.

Membership fees and training group times are managed through the Athletics Ireland registration portal. As of late 2025, the club has a significant waiting list for new juvenile members given the high demand.

Cuala GAA Club's Youth Academy, based at Hyde Park, Hyde Road, Dalkey, Co. Dublin, introduces children from age 5 up to the fundamentals of Gaelic football, hurling and camogie in a fun, structured environment at one of Dublin's largest GAA clubs.

Membership fees and academy training times are managed through the club's own registration system. The venue has both indoor and outdoor facilities with free parking.

De La Salle Palmerston FC runs mini rugby at Kirwan Park, Kilternan, Dublin 18, through IRFU-certified, Garda-vetted coaches at one of Leinster's oldest and largest mini-youth clubs. Daisy Pickers (ages 3-4) introduces the youngest children to basic movement and ball skills in a fun, non-contact format, while Minis (Under 6 to Under 12) builds age-appropriate rugby skills and teamwork as children progress.

Membership fees and training times are managed through the club's registration system. Outdoor venue with free parking.

David Scott has been teaching acting classes in Dublin for over 15 years, based at 1 Foley St, Dublin 1. His Applied Art of Acting approach runs across the Actors Wednesday Workshop, the Actors Friday Studio and a Summer Week Intensive, alongside online one-to-one training and corporate training sessions.

Full details are available at www.davidscott.ie, or by email at scottdavidmichael@gmail.com.

These acting workshops at Baldoyle Racecourse Community Centre, Dublin 13, take a no-nonsense approach to the craft, suited to actors of every level - including complete beginners keen to explore their creative side. Sessions cover character development, script analysis and delivering an authentic performance for stage and screen.

In a fun, safe space, the workshops also build communication skills, public speaking, self-confidence and resilience, encouraging participants to step outside their comfort zone with an open mind.

This adult beginner piano class offers a relaxed, supportive small-group setting in Kilbeggan, Co. Westmeath, personally led by Áine Nolan, PhD, who brings over 20 years of teaching experience. No prior experience is needed, and there's no age limit - just a weekly space to learn something new alongside like-minded adults.

Availability is limited, so email info@ainenolan.com to secure a place.

This afterschool service in Firhouse, Co. Dublin covers collection from school, homework support and a healthy snack, along with a mix of indoor and outdoor activities to keep children busy and entertained until pick-up.

Alizé's School of Singing, based at Danville Business Park, Ring Rd, Co. Kilkenny, is a music and performing arts school founded by Alizé Comerford, teaching children, teens and adults. Tuition covers singing, drama, musical theatre, piano, guitar, ukulele, pop choir and general performance training, all delivered in a supportive, encouraging environment aimed at building confidence and creativity alongside technical skill.

Playful Tribe's Afterschool Art Clubs are relaxed, process-led sessions held in a home studio in Bettystown, Co. Meath, where children explore materials like air-dry clay, watercolours, oil pastels, acrylics, drawing and mixed media while picking up professional tools and techniques. All materials are included.

Junior & Senior Infants meet on Mondays from 4 to 5.30pm, while 1st to 6th Class meet on Tuesdays, same time slot. It's a drop-off class best suited to children comfortable participating independently without one-to-one support. Classes run continuously through the year, so new starters can join whenever a space opens up in their group.

These children's art classes, held at Clonard Community Centre, Clonard Rd, Co. Wexford, cover painting, drawing and creative crafts in small, friendly groups with personal guidance from the instructor. They're aimed at building confidence and self-expression, suited to complete beginners as well as budding young artists.

Spaces are limited, so message ahead to book a spot or find out more.

Art in Layers, based on Camden Street Lower, Co. Dublin, is a studio focused on layered and textured art techniques. Workshops include Joomchi and Kinusaiga (traditional Korean and Japanese paper and fabric crafts), printmaking using recycled milk cartons, botanical collage with pressed flowers, pop-up card making and more - a good fit for anyone drawn to hands-on, tactile creative work.

Held at Studio 50 in Carnagh, Co. Armagh, BT60 3HZ, these relaxed art workshops give adults two hours of calm, creative time with professional artist Trish Redmond. Classes suit beginners, with guidance throughout so everyone leaves with a completed piece, and all materials are provided.

Come solo or bring a friend - tea, coffee and freshly baked treats are served alongside the making. Check Trish Redmond's social media for upcoming dates, or get in touch about private workshops at Studio 50.

Arty Party Place is a craft, birthday and pottery space at 6 Hynd's Square, Portlaoise, Co. Laois, at the rear of JBR Art Haus, the Midlands' largest craft supply store. Through the year it runs craft workshops, an afterschool craft club, kids' craft camps, pottery events and a drop-in pottery-painting venue, alongside partnerships with community groups and county councils across the Midlands for pottery, craft, crochet and upcycling sessions.

In-store birthday parties can be themed around pottery, pop stars, dinosaurs, Harry Potter, slime, Minecraft and more, or built to order, and a mobile craft party service is available to bring the workshop to your own venue. Adult workshops cover crochet, beginners' sewing, upcycling, candle and soap making, needle felting, floral wreaths, foraged balms and teas, pottery painting and handbuilding, foiling, alcohol ink art and polymer clay jewellery.

Brick Legends Ireland's kids' LEGO clubs use the world of LEGO bricks to build STEM-based creativity, imagination and a love of learning. Building and problem-solving with LEGO doubles as hands-on education in science, technology, engineering and maths, helping children develop cognitive, social and emotional skills while they play.

Babble & Bloom is a parent and baby early communication course held at Malahide Castle, Malahide Demesne, Co. Dublin, created and led by a registered Speech & Language Therapist. Over six weeks of relaxed, play-based sessions, parents learn evidence-based strategies for supporting communication from the very beginning - modelling baby signs, building connection and language through play, and turning everyday moments into opportunities to communicate.

It's suitable for babies and toddlers aged 6-14 months and gives parents a chance to build confidence in supporting their child's development while meeting others at a similar stage. Please note this is an educational class rather than a clinical Speech & Language Therapy service, and isn't a substitute for assessment or intervention where needed.

Emma, a registered nurse and midwife recently certified with the IAIM in infant massage, runs baby massage classes in Co. Louth from a private address. Each course consists of 5 classes for €150, and most private health insurers offer some level of reimbursement.

Get in touch by email at babymassageemma@gmail.com, or find Emma on Instagram at @babymassagewithemma to book.

Baby Sensory classes at St. Peter's GAA Dunboyne, Rooske Rd, Co. Meath, support babies' development from birth to 13 months through music, movement and sensory play - lights, textures, bubbles and more - all designed around early childhood development research. Each class is pitched to your baby's current stage, from tiny newborns to active explorers.

Beyond the developmental side, parents value the class as dedicated bonding time and a chance to meet other local families, in a warm, pressure-free environment.

Baby Sensory classes at the Keadeen Hotel, Co. Kildare, are suitable for babies from birth to 13 months and cover creative play, massage, tummy time, movement, visual development, textures, scents and music - all in simple, practical ways parents can easily repeat at home.

Original and traditional songs and rhymes help develop early speech and language skills, alongside sensory signing activities that let parents and babies start communicating from birth.

Barleyhill Icelandics, based in Barleyhill, Co. Cork, introduces children to the Icelandic horse - a breed known for its distinctive extra gaits alongside walk, trot and canter. It's a hands-on way for kids to learn about horses and riding in a setting built around this less common but gentle breed.

BeeWild for Kids offers an interactive beekeeping session covering hive equipment and basics, honey tastings, and sowing seeds to take home, plus the chance to meet the farm's hens, pigs, calves and chicks and go bee-spotting - tea and organic treats included. The BeeWild Combo builds on this with a fuller beekeeping setup (the hive as medicine, the matriarch bee, tree planting, weeds as wonders), a chicken setup (hatching, incubators, hygiene, the benefits of roosters) and a grow-your-own session covering weed suppression, natural fertiliser and pest prevention.

Separately, Forest Bathing sessions run in the on-site forest, combining a plant ID walk, nervous-system regulation and breathing practices, sensory exercises, guided visualisation and a closing tea circle in the woods.

Bloom Baby Classes, based near Pollamore, Co. Cavan, run two musical sensory programmes: Caterpillar Club for babies aged 0-6 months, and Busy Bees for babies aged 6-15 months. Caterpillar Club is a gentle, calming introduction to sensory play, using music, props, lights and movement, finishing with a chill parachute and short guided baby massage to encourage relaxation.

Busy Bees builds on those foundations with instruments, movement and props that support fine and gross motor skills, body awareness, early language and social interaction. Every week brings a new theme across a full year, with themed music, dress-up, sensory lights and treasure baskets giving both babies and parents plenty to explore - and plenty of chances for parents to relax, chat and build friendships within the Bloom community.

Boyne Babies runs sensory-rich classes for babies and toddlers up to age 2 at Julianstown Community Centre, Dimanistown West, Co. Meath. Weekly themed sessions bring together music, movement, lights, textures, messy play, soft play and other sensory activities tailored to different developmental stages, from non-walkers through to toddlers.

Beyond the developmental focus, it's also a welcoming space for parents to connect with other local families and enjoy some calm, engaging time together each week.

This 4-week children's art course runs from a studio in Tallaght, Dublin 24 (Partas, Brookfield Enterprise Centre, Rossfield Ave), for ages 5-11, Saturdays 12 to 1.30pm. All materials are provided for a fun, free-flow art and craft environment, at €60 for the full course.

McDermott Music, based in Clontarf, Dublin, offers Kodály-inspired early years music classes plus two choirs: the Clontarf Children's Choir (ages 7-12) and the Clontarf Youth Choir (ages 12-18). The programme was founded by qualified primary teacher and music educator Lauraine McDermott.

There are no auditions - the focus is on building confidence, musicianship and lasting friendships through singing, with performances and collaborations giving children a strong sense of community as they grow as young musicians.

Conscious Crafting runs inclusive crafting and visual arts workshops at Blue Door, River Cottage, Wells Lane, Gyles Quay, Ferrybank, Co. Louth, for ages 9 and up. Drawing on principles of art therapy, sessions use simple craft and art techniques built around conscious themes to encourage self-reflection, emotional expression and connection within a supportive, collaborative group.

This crochet club in Douglas, Cork brings together 9 to 13 year-olds to learn the craft in a relaxed, encouraging small-group setting - a chance to build a new skill while connecting with other young crafters in the local area.

Cuidiú Cork runs a regular calendar of parent, toddler, baby, breastfeeding and social meet-ups across Cork, from coffee mornings and playgroups to café meet-ups and breastfeeding support. Whether breastfeeding or bottle-feeding, working or at home, mums, dads, grandparents and carers are all welcome to join and connect with other local families while the children make friends of their own.

Full event listings and dates are kept up to date at cuidiucork.ie/cuidiú-cork-events.

Eoin's Guitar Lessons, based at 7 Ardán, Borrisokane, offers guitar and ukulele tuition locally as well as covering Nenagh, Cloughjordan and Portumna and the surrounding areas. Online lessons are also available for students anywhere.

This Expressive Arts Group meets every Thursday from 5 to 6pm at Glengoole Community Hall, Co. Tipperary, giving children a relaxed, supportive space to explore, imagine and express themselves. Sessions mix art, craft, sensory, movement and creative activities, with children encouraged to follow their own interests and build confidence in their choices and ideas along the way.

Running Thursdays in Glengoole, Co. Tipperary, this Expressive Arts group welcomes children from preschool age up to 10, in a one-hour drop-and-collect format. Sessions blend messy and process art with movement breaks, creative expression, emotional processing and friendship-building - a relaxed, low-pressure way for younger children to explore creativity together.

This one-day wet felting workshop at the Heritage Centre, Creggs, F42 X674, runs from 10am to 4pm and guides participants - beginners and more experienced felters alike - through designing and making a personalised felted handbag from start to finish. All materials are included, along with tea, coffee and cake.

By the end of the day you'll have a finished, handmade bag as well as the skills and confidence to keep exploring felting on your own.

This online fitness and music membership is designed for people of all abilities to train at their own pace, with two new on-demand sessions released each month plus a weekly live music-based movement class every Thursday from 5.30 to 6.15pm. Membership runs until cancelled and includes a 7-day free trial, making it easy to try before committing.

These kids' yoga classes are starting up in Mallow and Kanturk, North Cork, for children aged 4-12, run in 4-week blocks with limited spaces. Sessions are designed to help children build confidence, improve focus and learn to relax and unwind - useful skills alongside the physical practice of yoga itself.

Message via instagram.com/breatheandbloomkidsyoga to book a spot or find out more.

GCakes runs hands-on cake decorating workshops using cupcakes, cookies and cakes, tailored around birthdays and other events. Every guest leaves with their own decorated creations plus a box of handmade treats, with all utensils and tools supplied and decorating themes matched to the group's age and interests.

Children's workshops are pitched to suit different ages and skill levels, with hands-on guidance throughout, while Tween & Teen Workshops (12+) go a step further into piping, sugar paste, 3D models and more advanced techniques. Note these are decorating rather than baking classes - the baked items are supplied ready to decorate, and allergens aren't catered for as items are baked and stored where nuts are also present. Private events can be arranged at a location of your choice in Dublin.

These Irish baking and cooking classes run from a country home in Kilcolgan, on Galway's west coast, covering everything from scone and bread making to Irish stew, apple pie and Irish coffee. Menus can be personalised around specific dishes or dietary requirements on request.

Classes run for about two hours with a maximum of six people, finishing with tea or coffee to enjoy the results of the session. Email galwaycookeryclasses@gmail.com to book.
